The format of Reddit I think is one of the best ways to create a site that will pull people in since any type of content can be shared, users can customize what they see and discussion is easy. Voat takes that format and the change here is the community and the mods dedication to free speech (although early reddit was also hugely pro free speech, we will see how that goes).

On reddit the primary attitude is that number of subscribers is the most important thing, so anything that gains subscribers gets done. To aid this, moderators are essentially gods of their subreddits - they can do no wrong. And since they have the ability to silence critics, there's no way to tell if a lot of people are unhappy with a sub's moderation.

By catering to anyone who whines, generally subreddits end up with a bunch of mindless rules that are applied inconsistently, and a bunch of moderators who make shit up as they go along. They also tolerate zero challenge to their authority - arguing with a mod is usually the fasted way to get banned from a sub.

In general, Voat is trying not to use censorship as a tool as much. There are still some subverses with silly rules - most notable is /v/pics, which was set up by someone to wanted it to be /v/photos, so lots of folks who submit pictures there that aren't photos get their submissions deleted (including the founder of Voat).
